[[File:Fancy boots detail.png|120px|left]]
'''Fancy boots''' are a pair of low level boots with stats identical to [[bronze boots]] (except weighing significantly less), [[fighting boots]] and [[fancier boots]]. They are obtained from the [[Cradle of Life]] on the fourth level of the [[Stronghold of Security]] dungeon provided the player's account has two-factor authentication enabled. They are used by new or [[free-to-play]] players, as the centre of each level rewards a combined total of {{NoCoins|10000}} [[coins]] along with the choice between fancy boots, fighting boots or fancier boots (at the fourth and final level).

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the [[gravestone]]. When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the [[Cradle of Life]]. Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

They used to be the best melee [[boots]] in free-to-play, but have since been surpassed by all of the [[Castle Wars]] [[decorative boots]], especially the [[decorative boots (gold)]] due to their [[Strength bonus]]. The high requirement of 400 [[castle wars tickets]] causes the fancy boots to still be popular, due to its nonexistent cost.

==Changes==
{{Subject changes header}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 1 November 2023
|update = Forestry Tweaks, Security & More
|change = 
* Players may now own an unlimited number of fancy boots.
* Fancy boots are no longer destroyed, but rather dropped.
* Players may now own both fancy boots and [[fighting boots]].
* Players who have a [[Jagex Account]] can now combine fancy boots with fighter boots to obtain [[fancier boots]].
* Fancy boots can now be stored in the [[armour case space]] of the [[costume room]] in a [[player-owned house]].
}}
